title.narrative: Strengthen Pacific Media in Climate Action and Disaster Management

description.narrative:
Member States in the Pacific region will be supported, through strengthened media institutions, in their efforts for climate adaptation and disaster preparedness and response. This will be achieved primarily by improving the institutional strategies, competencies, and practices of media to effectively inform and engage the public on issues related to climate change and disasters. Media will be equipped to go beyond being mere conduits for expert and scientific message, and instead report on the actions or inactions of social actors regarding environmental degradation. Media will be better able to use public information sources, artificial intelligence and other digital tools for data gathering, analysis, and content production. With enhanced access to reliable media content throughout the disaster management cycle, from prevention and preparedness to response and recovery, people, particularly the most vulnerable, will be better equipped to make informed decisions, and more resilient in the face of extreme weather events and disasters.
The workplan will strengthen media institutions in the Pacific, a region with low-lying islands and diverse ecosystems that is particularly vulnerable to climate change and disasters. Media will have a greater impact on climate action and disaster preparedness and response in the region, not only by providing essential information but mostly by facilitating public debates, uncovering disaster risks, and discussing solutions to challenges across national borders.
